project_requirements.title: What the call wants
project_requirements.question: What must the project address, develop and achieve?

cards.title: Central object
cards.question: What is the principal thing the project must develop?
cards.answer:
A one-year public-private partnership research programme (PPS-programma) of a Top Consortium for Knowledge and Innovation, starting 1 January 2027, carried out through collaborative research projects and support activities for SMEs.
A Top Consortium for Knowledge and Innovation (TKI) is one of 12 foundations named in the budget of the Ministry of Economic Affairs that organise research cooperation between companies and knowledge institutions in a field, for example TKI Energie. The call does not fund a project directly: it gives the TKI a programme subsidy (PPS-programmasubsidie), which the TKI must then spend only on:
- collaborative projects (samenwerkingsprojecten) of fundamental research, industrial research, experimental development or a combination, carried out in real cooperation by at least one research organisation and one company;
- innovation activities that bring SMEs into the projects or spread the knowledge: open network activities (masterclasses, workshops, conferences, a website) and innovation advice to SMEs by an innovation broker.
The programme must set out the TKI's research course within one or more Knowledge and Innovation Agendas (KIAs, multi-year agendas of research goals per field).
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · Artikel 3.2.1 Begripsomschrijvingen; Artikel 3.2.2 Aanvraag

cards.title: Scope
cards.question: Which activities fall within the funding opportunity's scope?
cards.answer:
In scope are collaborative research projects and SME support activities that fit the TKI's programme; projects that have already started are excluded.
In scope:
- Collaborative projects of fundamental research, industrial research (research to gain new knowledge for new products or processes) or experimental development (building and testing prototypes or pilots), or a combination.
- Network activities open to every SME, such as masterclasses, workshops, conferences or a knowledge-sharing website.
- Innovation advice services to SMEs by an innovation broker, excluding training.
Excluded or restricted:
- A project, or part of it, that has started, or will start, before the TKI allocates the subsidy to it.
- Projects without real cooperation, or that do not contribute to the Dutch knowledge infrastructure or to the PPS programme.
- Training within innovation advice services.
The call sets no subject restrictions of its own: the subjects follow from the KIAs the TKI chooses, so for energy topics the programme of TKI Energie is decisive.

cards.title: Problem
cards.question: What type of problem or need must justify the project, and where must it originate?
cards.answer:
The project must address research that is socially and economically relevant in the medium to long term, as set out in the Knowledge and Innovation Agendas.
The scheme has two aims: to stimulate cooperation between knowledge institutions and companies within the top sectors (the fields the Dutch government singles out for innovation policy) on such research, and to strengthen research aimed at the KIAs, which serve the goals of mission-driven innovation policy (Dutch policy that steers research towards societal missions such as the energy transition). The need is shared by companies and the research community in the TKI's field; the TKI must explain in its programme how it identifies and selects projects that fit.

cards.title: Impact
cards.question: Which wider system outcomes and impacts must the project support?
cards.answer:
The programme must contribute to the Knowledge and Innovation Agendas and the goals of mission-driven innovation policy, and strengthen the Dutch knowledge infrastructure.
- A programme that contributes too little to the KIAs it names is rejected.
- Each funded project must contribute to the Dutch knowledge infrastructure.
- The TKI must work to make private contributions (cash and in-kind) as large as possible and may set out how it draws SMEs into projects.
The call sets no quantified targets and no energy-system outcomes of its own.

PPS Innovatie (RVO page) · Doel

cards.title: After the project
cards.question: How must the result be replicated, taken up and kept in use after the project?
cards.answer:
The call requires that results be shared and applied, not that they become operational or commercial products.
- The TKI must promote that knowledge from research commissioned with programme subsidy is actually applied within a collaborative project of the programme.
- The TKI must publish the non-confidential knowledge and information gained in the projects.
- In each project, the company must obtain the rights to the research organisation's results at market price, or rights that reflect its work packages, contributions and interests; this must be set out in a signed collaboration agreement.
The call does not require replication, standards or someone to operate the results after funding ends.

cards.title: Number of partners
cards.question: What is the permitted or required consortium size?
cards.answer: Each collaborative project needs at least two participants: one research organisation and one company. The call sets no maximum.
cards.sources: Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · Artikel 3.2.1 Begripsomschrijvingen (samenwerkingsproject)

cards.title: Partner composition
cards.question: Which types of partners must the consortium include?
cards.answer:
Each project must include at least one research organisation and at least one company; SMEs are encouraged.
- The TKI must let companies and research organisations join projects under transparent and reasonable conditions, which it publishes.
- The TKI may describe how it will draw SMEs into projects; network activities must be open to all SMEs or involve at least one SME per EUR 1,000 of subsidy.
- Projects must contribute to the Dutch knowledge infrastructure; the call sets no other country rule for partners.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · Artikel 3.2.1; Artikel 3.2.5, eerste lid, onderdeel f, en vierde lid; Artikel 3.2.6, tweede lid, onderdeel d, onder 6°
PPS Innovatie: Voorwaarden inzet programmasubsidie (RVO page) · Algemene voorwaarden

cards.title: Distribution of work
cards.question: How must work and budget be distributed among partners?
cards.answer:
Work, contributions and intellectual property must be set out per participant in a signed collaboration agreement, and aid per participant is capped.
- The project must be carried out in real cooperation.
- The agreement must state the cash contribution (private bijdrage, money not from a research organisation or public body) and in-kind contribution (private inzet in natura, valued work or resources) of each participant, and how intellectual property is handled.
- The TKI reports the eligible costs and the subsidy it allocates per participant.
- Aid per participant may not exceed the EU notification threshold; RVO states this is met in any case below EUR 5 million of programme subsidy per company.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · Artikel 3.2.1; Artikel 3.2.5, eerste lid, onderdelen a, d en g; Artikel 3.2.7, onderdelen d tot en met g
PPS Innovatie: Voorwaarden inzet programmasubsidie (RVO page) · Algemene voorwaarden

cards.title: Coordinator
cards.question: What type of organisation may or must act as lead applicant?
cards.answer:
Only a TKI may apply: one of the 12 Top Consortia for Knowledge and Innovation in the budget of the Ministry of Economic Affairs.
These are TKI AgriFood, Groene Chemie and Circulariteit, ClickNL (creative industry), Energie, High Tech Systems and Materials, Life Sciences and Health, Logistiek, Tuinbouw en Uitgangsmaterialen, Maritiem, Deltatechnologie, Watertechnologie and ICT. The call does not say who leads an individual collaborative project; that is up to the TKI's conditions.

project_requirements.title: TenneT's position
project_requirements.question: What is TenneT's position within the consortium?

cards.title: Coordinate
cards.question: Can TenneT apply or coordinate, and under which conditions?
cards.answer:
No. Only a TKI may apply for the programme subsidy, so TenneT cannot apply or coordinate.
TenneT could at most propose or lead a collaborative project inside the programme of a TKI, most likely TKI Energie, if that TKI's published participation conditions allow it; the call itself does not regulate who leads a project.
cards.sources: Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · Artikel 3.2.2 Aanvraag; Artikel 3.2.10, eerste lid, onderdeel c

cards.title: Participate
cards.question: Can TenneT take part without receiving funding?
cards.answer:
Yes. TenneT can join a collaborative project of a TKI as a company partner, contributing knowledge and money.
RVO describes the route: companies take part in a project of a TKI's programme, share knowledge, risk and investment, and contribute knowledge and money; in return they get extra research because the government adds programme subsidy. TenneT would communicate with the TKI about its project, and the TKI deals with RVO. Its contribution would count as a private cash contribution or in-kind contribution under the collaboration agreement. To take part, TenneT contacts the TKI concerned, for energy topics TKI Energie.
cards.sources:
PPS Innovatie: Deelnemen aan een PPS-project (RVO page) · Introduction; Contact met TKI's
PPS Innovatie (RVO page) · Deelnemen aan een project in het PPS-programma

cards.title: Receive funding
cards.question: Can TenneT receive funding, and which funding rate or cost rules apply?
cards.answer:
Possibly, but it depends on the TKI: the TKI decides how much subsidy each project participant receives, within caps per type of research.
The TKI reports the subsidy it allocates per participant, so a company such as TenneT TSO B.V. can in principle receive part of it. Aid per participant may not exceed:
- Fundamental research: 80% of eligible costs
- Industrial research: 50%, or 60% when the collaboration conditions of EU rules are met (RVO states 60%)
- Experimental development: 25%, or 40% under the same conditions (RVO states 40%)
Eligible costs are personnel, equipment and buildings (depreciation during the project), contract research and patents, and overheads and materials. RVO describes the company's role mainly as contributing money and knowledge in return for extra research, so TenneT should expect to finance most or all of its own costs unless TKI Energie's project conditions allocate subsidy to it. The TKI Energie budget for this round is EUR 17,288,143.

cards.title: TenneT's likely contribution
cards.question: What contribution would make TenneT credible and useful within the project?
cards.answer:
Our judgement: TenneT would be most credible as a co-funding company partner in TKI Energie research projects on grid operation and system integration.
TenneT could bring research questions from grid operation, grid data, access to test and simulation environments such as the National Facility Digital Twin of the Electricity System, and specialist knowledge, building on the university-led work it already supports in TenneTwin and the digital twin programme with NWO. Its cash or in-kind contribution would raise the private share the TKI must maximise, and a seat in the project's user or steering group would let it shape the research. Whether this route suits TenneT depends on TKI Energie's programme topics and participation conditions, which are not part of this call.

project_requirements.title: Innovation
project_requirements.question: What type of innovation must the project develop?

cards.title: Innovation threshold
cards.question: Must the project produce genuinely new knowledge or technology, or may it integrate and apply existing solutions?
cards.answer:
The projects must produce new knowledge: only fundamental research, industrial research and experimental development may be funded.
Applying existing solutions without research is outside the definition of a collaborative project. Innovation activities for SMEs (network events and advice) are the exception: they spread knowledge rather than create it.
cards.sources: Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · Artikel 3.2.1 Begripsomschrijvingen (samenwerkingsproject, innovatieactiviteiten)

cards.title: Innovation object
cards.question: In what must the project innovate?
cards.answer: The call does not restrict what the research must innovate in; the subject follows from the KIAs the TKI chooses and the TKI's programme.
cards.sources: Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · Artikel 3.2.1 (PPS-programma, KIA); Artikel 3.2.6, tweede lid, onderdeel d

cards.title: Development stages
cards.question: Which development stages must the project cover?
cards.answer:
Fundamental research, industrial research and experimental development, alone or combined; deployment is not funded.
- Fundamental research: work to gain new basic knowledge without a direct application in view.
- Industrial research: research to gain new knowledge for new or clearly improved products, processes or services.
- Experimental development: building and testing prototypes, pilots or demonstrations close to real use.
The aid caps differ per stage (80%, 50–60% and 25–40%), so the mix of stages shapes the funding.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · Artikel 3.2.1; Artikel 3.2.5, eerste lid, onderdeel d
PPS Innovatie: Voorwaarden inzet programmasubsidie (RVO page) · Maximale steun

cards.title: Maturity
cards.question: Which maturity level is expected at the start and end of the project?
cards.answer: The call sets no TRL (technology readiness level) for the start or end of projects; the stages it funds run from basic research up to prototype testing in experimental development.
cards.sources: Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · Artikel 3.2.1; Artikel 3.2.5

project_requirements.title: Work
project_requirements.question: Which activities or work structure must the project cover?

cards.title: Demonstration
cards.question: Where and under which conditions must the solution be demonstrated?

cards.title: Integration
cards.question: How must the activities fit together and with existing systems?
cards.answer:
Each project must fit the TKI's programme and the KIAs, and may also link to the field of other TKIs.
- The TKI may only fund projects that contribute to its PPS programme.
- A TKI that wants to fund projects touching the field and KIAs of other TKIs must explain how it will do so.
- Existing funding of activities taken into the programme must stay in place.
The call says nothing about integration with existing infrastructure or processes.

funding_timing_submission.title: Funding
funding_timing_submission.question: How much funding can the project receive?

cards.title: Funding envelope
cards.answer:
Each TKI has its own budget ceiling for this round, together about EUR 165.5 million; TKI Energie can receive up to EUR 17,288,143.
- Total project size: the call sets none; the TKI decides the size of its projects.
- Grant request: per TKI, up to its ceiling, for example TKI Energie EUR 17,288,143, TKI HTSM EUR 39,193,745, Life Sciences and Health EUR 59,057,112, TKI ICT EUR 4,990,003 and TKI Groene Chemie en Circulariteit EUR 8,068,051.
- Funding form: a programme subsidy to the TKI, which it spends on actual eligible costs of projects and activities.
cards.sources:
Staatscourant 2026, 37215 · Artikel II; Toelichting § 1 Aanleiding
PPS Innovatie (RVO page) · Hoogte subsidie en aanvraagperiode

cards.title: Funding rate and co-financing
cards.answer:
Aid rates depend on the type of research and the participant; companies must also bring their own cash or in-kind contribution.
- Fundamental research: up to 80% of eligible costs per participant
- Industrial research: up to 50%, or 60% under the EU collaboration conditions
- Experimental development: up to 25%, or 40% under the EU collaboration conditions
- Research organisations, non-economic activities: up to 80%
- Network activities: up to 100% of third-party costs
- Innovation advice: up to 100%, at most EUR 10,000 per SME per year, for at most three years
- Co-financing conditions: private cash contributions and in-kind contributions per participant, set out in the collaboration agreement; money from research organisations or public bodies does not count as private.
- Evidence required: a signed collaboration agreement showing each participant's contribution.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · Artikel 3.2.1; Artikel 3.2.5
PPS Innovatie: Voorwaarden inzet programmasubsidie (RVO page) · Maximale steun; Subsidiabele kosten en maximale steunintensiteit

cards.title: Budget constraints
cards.answer:
Eligible costs follow the EU research aid rules, with caps per company and on advice services.
- Eligible costs: personnel (researchers, technicians, support staff), equipment and buildings as depreciation during the project, contract research, knowledge and patents bought at market terms, consultancy, and overheads and materials.
- Caps or mandatory allocations: aid below the EU notification threshold per participant (in any case met below EUR 5 million per company); innovation advice in total at most EUR 300,000 a year, or EUR 200,000 plus 0.5% of the subsidy when 0.5% is EUR 100,000 or more (the RVO page states lower limits of EUR 100,000 or 0.5%).
- Excluded costs: network activities may only pay third-party costs; training is not eligible in advice services.
cards.sources:

funding_timing_submission.title: Timing
funding_timing_submission.question: What timing should the proposal submission and project follow?

cards.title: Application route
cards.answer:
One stage: the TKI applies online in Mijn RVO with eHerkenning, from 2 November 2026, 09:00, to 31 December 2026, 17:00.
- Stage 1 — Application by the TKI: by 31 December 2026, 17:00, with the attachment Format aanvraag PPS-programmasubsidie 2027 and eHerkenning level 2+ with authorisation for RVO services at eH2+.
- Additional procedure: a company such as TenneT does not apply to RVO; it joins through the TKI's own project selection, so it must contact TKI Energie, which sets its own conditions and timing.
cards.sources:
PPS Innovatie (RVO page) · Hoogte subsidie en aanvraagperiode; Uw aanvraag voorbereiden; Aanvragen
Staatscourant 2026, 37215 · Artikel II

cards.title: Project window
cards.answer:
The programme starts on 1 January 2027 and the subsidy must be used within six years of the grant.
- Required start: the TKI must name its projects within 18 months of the programme start; a project may not start before the TKI allocates the subsidy to it.
- Eligible-cost period: within six years of the grant.
- Completion deadline: the TKI applies for final settlement within 13 weeks of the end date of the programme subsidy.
The current scheme ends at the end of 2027; from 2028 a new scheme starts under which project proposals go to RVO instead of the TKIs.

cards.title: Decision and contracting
cards.answer:
RVO decides per TKI on a first-come, first-served basis; projects need a signed collaboration agreement before the subsidy is used.
- Funding decision: no date stated; the ceilings are allocated in order of receipt.
- Conditions before starting: a collaboration agreement signed by all parties, setting out each participant's contributions and the handling of intellectual property, at the latest when the TKI allocates the subsidy to the project.
cards.sources: Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · Artikel 3.2.3 Verdeling van subsidieplafonds; Artikel 3.2.5, eerste lid, onderdeel g; Artikel 3.2.7, onderdeel e

funding_timing_submission.title: Application
funding_timing_submission.question: Mandatory information to include in the application

cards.title: Mandatory submission package — pass/fail
cards.answer:
The TKI's application must contain its details, the amount requested and the PPS programme description.
- Application form: online in Mijn RVO, with the Format aanvraag PPS-programmasubsidie 2027 (Word) attached.
- Mandatory annexes: the programme, describing the KIAs it serves, how projects are selected, how private contributions are maximised, how transparency is ensured, and any cross-TKI work, SME involvement and innovation activities.
- Registration: Chamber of Commerce number and eHerkenning level 2+.
cards.sources:
Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · Artikel 3.2.6 Informatieverplichtingen bij subsidieaanvraag
PPS Innovatie (RVO page) · Uw aanvraag voorbereiden; Aanvragen

cards.title: Evaluation and selection — scored or ranked
cards.answer:
Applications are not scored: RVO rejects a programme only if it contributes too little to its KIAs or is of insufficient quality.
- Evaluation criteria: contribution to the named KIAs; quality of how the programme works out the required topics.
- Ranking rules: first come, first served within each TKI's ceiling.
cards.sources: Regeling nationale EZ-, LVVN- en KGG-subsidies (wetten.overheid.nl, version 6 May 2026) · Artikel 3.2.3; Artikel 3.2.4 Afwijzingsgronden

cards.title: Conditional and exceptional requirements
cards.answer:
Several obligations follow the grant, mainly for the TKI.
- Conditional — project lasts longer than 12 months: the TKI reports progress once a year, with its annual report.
- Conditional — programme subsidy of EUR 125,000 or more: the final settlement needs an auditor's report.
- Conditional — essential changes (content, delays, budget changes above 25%, parts not carried out): the TKI must report them to RVO.
- Recommended: companies that want to take part should contact the relevant TKI directly.
